title: Adjective agreement
description: Make the describing word match the noun.

guide.summary: An adjective in French copies the noun it describes: feminine or masculine, one or several. This topic gives you the endings, the irregular ones, and the cases where nothing changes at all.

sections.title: The four forms of an adjective
sections.text: Most adjectives build all their forms from the masculine singular: add e for the feminine, s for the plural, es for both.
steps: Find the noun the adjective describes.
Masculine or feminine? Un and le mark masculine, une and la mark feminine.
One or several? Des and les mark the plural.
Take that line of the table and add its ending.
watch: Des and les say plural but say nothing about gender: the exercise tells you whether the noun is masculine or feminine.
Most of these endings are silent: petit and petits sound alike, so check the spelling with your eyes, not your ear.
Where the adjective sits, before or after the noun, is another topic; leave it where the sentence puts it.

sections.title: Adjectives that already end in e
sections.text: An adjective whose masculine form already ends in e does not change in the feminine. It still takes s in the plural.
steps: Look at the last letter of the masculine form.
If it is already e, write nothing extra for a feminine noun.
Add s all the same when the noun is plural.
watch: Never write a second e: rougee, jeunee and facilee do not exist.
The plural s is still owed: mes frères sont calmes.

sections.title: -eux, -if, -er: feminines that swap the ending
sections.text: These three endings do not simply take an e. The whole ending changes.
steps: Check the noun’s gender first: only a feminine noun triggers this.
Read the last letters of the masculine form.
Swap the whole ending; do not glue an e onto it.
Add s on top for a plural noun: heureuses, sportives, chères.
watch: Heureuse, not heureuxe; sportive, not sportife.
The -er feminine needs a grave accent: chère, première, dernière.

sections.title: Endings that double their consonant
sections.text: Adjectives in -en, -on and -el double their last consonant before the feminine e, and so does gentil.
steps: Check that the noun is feminine.
Spot the ending: -en, -on, -el, or gentil.
Double that last consonant, then add e.
Count your letters: one n or one l is the usual slip.
watch: Italiene, bone and traditionnele are all missing a letter.
The doubling is audible: bon and bonne are not pronounced the same way.
Mignon follows the same line: mignonne.

sections.title: Irregular feminines to learn by heart
sections.text: A few common adjectives rebuild their feminine. There is no rule: learn each pair as one word.
steps: Check that the noun is feminine.
Ask whether the adjective is one of these irregular ones before you write anything.
Write the memorised feminine, not the masculine plus e.
Add s on top for a plural noun: blanches, longues.
watch: The feminine of frais is not fraise: une fraise is a strawberry.
The u in longue keeps the hard g sound.
Fraîche may also be spelled fraiche in the reformed spelling.

sections.title: The masculine plural: -aux, -eaux, or nothing
sections.text: The feminine plural is always regular. Only the masculine plural holds surprises.
steps: Only ask this question when the noun is masculine and plural.
Read the last letters of the masculine singular and take the matching line.
For a feminine plural noun, ignore this table: add e, then s.
watch: Loyaux and normaux, never loyals or normals.
A word already ending in s or x takes no second plural letter: heureuxs does not exist.
The -aux plural is masculine only; the feminine stays regular: loyale, loyales.
Nouns behave the same way: un journal, des journaux; un gâteau, des gâteaux.

sections.title: Colour words that never change
sections.text: A colour word that is also the name of a thing keeps one single form, whatever the noun.
steps: Ask whether the colour is also the name of an object, a fruit or a nut.
If it is, copy it exactly: no e, no s, for any noun.
Ordinary colour words still take the usual endings.
watch: You will see des sacs oranges written; the standard rule keeps this colour invariable.
Rose and mauve are exceptions to the exception: they do agree (des robes roses).

sections.title: Two nouns together: which form?
sections.text: When one adjective describes several nouns, the gender of the whole group decides.
steps: List everyone or everything the adjective describes.
If at least one of them is masculine, use the masculine plural.
Keep the feminine plural only when every member of the group is feminine.

examples.fr: Mon frère et ma sœur sont grands.
examples.en: My brother and my sister are tall.

watch: One man in the group is enough to cancel the feminine ending.
The verb goes plural too: sont, not est.

steps: Check the article: une or la means feminine singular.
Take the masculine form and add e.
Add nothing else: a single noun takes no plural s.
Confirm the noun is masculine and names more than one thing.
Add s to the masculine form.
Leave out the e: that mark belongs to feminine nouns only.
Confirm the noun is feminine and plural.
Build the feminine form first, then add the plural s.
Check that both marks are there before you submit.
Look at the masculine form: does it already end in e?
If it does, write it unchanged for a feminine noun.
Add s only when the noun is plural.
Check the noun’s gender first.
Read the last letters of the masculine form: -eux, -if or -er.
Swap the whole ending instead of adding a letter.
Add s at the very end if the noun is plural.
Check that the noun is feminine.
Spot the ending -en, -on or -el (and gentil).
Double the last consonant, then add e.
Re-read your spelling: the doubled letter is what learners drop.
Check that the noun is feminine.
Ask whether this adjective is one of the irregular ones before writing.
Write the memorised feminine rather than the masculine plus e.
Check the noun: is it masculine as well as plural?
If the masculine singular ends in -al use -aux; if it ends in -eau use -eaux.
If the noun is feminine, forget -aux and build the regular feminine plural.
Check the noun is masculine and plural.
Look at the last letter of the masculine singular.
If it is already s or x, copy the adjective exactly as it is.
Ask whether the colour word is also the name of a thing, a fruit or a nut.
If it is, copy it letter for letter, whatever the noun.
Other colours still take the usual feminine and plural endings.
List everyone the adjective describes.
If one of them is masculine, use the masculine plural.
Keep the feminine plural only when the whole group is feminine.

exercises.instruction: Replace un sac with une chaussure and make noir agree. Write the whole phrase.
exercises.hint: Une tells you chaussure is feminine singular. What does noir need to match it?
exercises.feedback: The new noun is feminine singular. Check the adjective’s ending as well as the noun replacement.
exercises.explanation: Changing the noun to the feminine chaussure requires noire. The adjective keeps its place after the noun.

mistakes.why: The noun was replaced but the adjective was left in its masculine form. A feminine singular noun needs the feminine mark on the adjective too.
Une was asked for because the noun is feminine; un marks a masculine noun.
The s marks several items. Une tells you there is exactly one shoe here.

exercises.instruction: Build the phrase with the correct form of rond. Table is feminine singular. Leave the other adjective tiles unused.
exercises.hint: Table is feminine singular. The adjective needs the feminine ending, but nothing for the plural.
exercises.feedback: Choose just one adjective tile. It must match a feminine noun with only one item.
exercises.explanation: Rond gains e for the feminine singular noun table. Une also shows that the noun is feminine singular.

mistakes.why: That tile is the plain masculine form, the one a dictionary lists. Une table is feminine, so the adjective needs its feminine mark.
That tile carries a plural s and no feminine mark at all, while the noun is one single feminine thing.
That tile marks feminine and plural at once. There is only one table on the prompt.

exercises.instruction: Fill the blank with the correct form of petit. Write only the adjective.
exercises.hint: Une tells you maison is feminine singular.
exercises.feedback: Check the adjective’s feminine ending. The noun is singular, so no plural ending is needed.
exercises.explanation: Petit gains e to agree with the feminine singular noun maison. It stays before the noun in this phrase.

mistakes.why: That is the masculine form, straight from the dictionary. Une maison is feminine, so the adjective needs its feminine ending.
That form is feminine but plural. Une shows there is only one house.
The s marks several items and there is no feminine mark; maison is one feminine noun.

exercises.instruction: Fix the adjective so it agrees with voiture. Keep the other words unchanged.
exercises.hint: Une shows feminine singular. What is the feminine form of vert?
exercises.feedback: The article shows feminine singular. Make the adjective match those two features.
exercises.explanation: Verte is the feminine singular form of vert. There is one car, so do not add a plural s.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence exactly as given: the adjective is still masculine, while une voiture is feminine singular.
An s was added instead of the feminine mark. There is one car, and it is feminine.
That ending is feminine plural. Une tells you there is a single car.

exercises.instruction: Make the whole phrase plural, replacing un with des. Sac is masculine.
exercises.hint: In the plural, both the noun and the adjective take the regular plural ending.
exercises.feedback: Make both the noun and adjective plural, and replace the singular article as requested.
exercises.explanation: Petits agrees with the masculine plural noun sacs. No feminine e is needed.

mistakes.why: The noun went plural but the adjective stayed singular. The adjective copies the number of its noun.
The adjective is plural but the noun is not. Both words take the plural ending.
That adjective form is feminine. Sac is a masculine noun, so no e belongs on it.

exercises.instruction: Build the phrase with the correct form of vert. Livres is masculine plural. Leave the other adjective tiles unused.
exercises.hint: The adjective needs a plural s but no feminine e.
exercises.feedback: Choose just one adjective tile. It must be plural without a feminine ending.
exercises.explanation: Vert becomes verts to describe more than one masculine livre.

mistakes.why: That tile is the singular masculine form. Livres names more than one book.
That tile is feminine singular: an e and no plural mark. The noun is masculine and plural.
That tile is feminine plural. Livre is a masculine noun, so the e does not belong.

exercises.instruction: Fill the blank with the correct form of noir. Sacs is masculine plural. Write only the adjective.
exercises.hint: Start with noir and add the regular plural ending.
exercises.feedback: The noun is masculine and names more than one item. Check both features of your adjective.
exercises.explanation: The adjective agrees with masculine plural sacs, so noir gains s but not e.

mistakes.why: That is the singular form. Sacs names several bags, so the plural ending is missing.
The e makes it feminine singular. Sacs is masculine and there is more than one.
That is the feminine plural: the number is right, but sac is a masculine noun.

exercises.instruction: Fix only the adjective. Chats is masculine plural.
exercises.hint: Chats already has its plural s. Give noir one too.
exercises.feedback: The noun is already plural. Check whether the adjective also marks the plural.
exercises.explanation: Noirs agrees with masculine plural chats. Des alone does not show gender; the prompt supplies it.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged: the noun has its plural s but the adjective has nothing.
The plural mark moved to the adjective and left the noun singular. Both words are plural here.
That adjective is feminine plural. The prompt says chats is masculine, so the e is wrong.

exercises.instruction: Make the whole phrase plural, replacing une with des. Maison is feminine.
exercises.hint: The adjective already shows the feminine. Now the adjective and the noun both need the plural ending.
exercises.feedback: Keep the adjective feminine while making both it and the noun plural. Remember to change the article.
exercises.explanation: Petites agrees with feminine plural maisons. Its ending has both e for feminine and s for plural.

mistakes.why: The noun went plural but the adjective stayed singular. Both words take the plural ending.
The adjective is plural but the noun was left singular; des asks for a plural noun.
That adjective is masculine plural. Maison is feminine, so the feminine mark must stay.

exercises.instruction: Build the phrase with the correct form of rond. Tables is feminine plural. Leave the other adjective tiles unused.
exercises.hint: The adjective needs both the feminine e and the plural s.
exercises.feedback: Choose just one adjective tile. Its ending must show both feminine and plural.
exercises.explanation: Rond becomes rondes for feminine plural tables: add e, then s.

mistakes.why: That tile is feminine singular. Tables names several tables, so the plural mark is missing.
That tile is masculine plural. Table is a feminine noun, so the feminine mark is missing.
That tile is the bare masculine singular, with neither mark, while the noun carries both.

exercises.instruction: Fill the blank with the correct form of vert. Voitures is feminine plural. Write only the adjective.
exercises.hint: Start from the feminine form of vert, then make it plural.
exercises.feedback: Check both gender and number: the noun is feminine and refers to more than one item.
exercises.explanation: Vertes matches both the feminine gender and the plural number of voitures.

mistakes.why: That is the feminine singular. Voitures names more than one car.
That is the masculine plural. Voiture is a feminine noun, so the feminine mark is missing.
That is the plain masculine singular, with neither mark. The noun is feminine and plural.

exercises.instruction: Fix only the adjective. Chaussures is feminine plural.
exercises.hint: Noir must match both feminine and plural.
exercises.feedback: The adjective must reflect two features of the noun: feminine gender and plural number.
exercises.explanation: Noires has the feminine e and the plural s required by chaussures.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged: the adjective carries neither mark, while chaussures is feminine and plural.
The adjective is feminine but singular. Chaussures names several shoes.
The plural s is there but the feminine mark is not. Chaussure is a feminine noun.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of cher.
exercises.hint: Jupe is feminine singular. Adjectives ending in -er change more than just adding e.
exercises.feedback: Look for the feminine singular form, and check the accent it needs.
exercises.explanation: Cher becomes chère in the feminine: -er turns into -ère, with a grave accent. Jupe is feminine singular, so no s.

mistakes.why: That is the masculine singular, the dictionary form. Jupe is feminine, and -er adjectives take a grave accent on the e before r.
That form is masculine and plural. The sentence is about one single skirt.
The feminine spelling is right but the s makes it plural. Cette jupe is one skirt.

exercises.instruction: Write heureux in the form that agrees with Léa. Write only the adjective.
exercises.hint: Léa is one woman. Adjectives ending in -eux have their own feminine ending.
exercises.feedback: Adding e to heureux does not work. Think of the feminine of -eux adjectives.
exercises.explanation: The -eux ending becomes -euse in the feminine: heureux, heureuse.

mistakes.why: That is the masculine form. Léa is one woman, and -eux adjectives take their own feminine ending.
This glues an e onto the masculine -eux. The x itself has to change in the feminine.
The feminine ending is right, but the s makes it plural and Léa is one person.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.hint: Sœur is feminine. Adjectives ending in -if change their last letter in the feminine.
exercises.feedback: Check the ending of sportif: the feminine is not sportife.
exercises.explanation: The -if ending becomes -ive in the feminine: sportif, sportive.

mistakes.why: Sportif is the masculine form. Sœur is feminine, and -if adjectives change their ending in the feminine.
Adding e to the masculine -if is the usual guess, but the f itself has to change.
Sœur is a feminine noun, so the possessive in front of it must be the feminine one.

exercises.instruction: Fix the adjective.
exercises.hint: Grand-mère is feminine. What happens to -if in the feminine?
exercises.feedback: The adjective is still in its masculine form. Change its ending, not the noun.
exercises.explanation: Actif becomes active for a feminine noun: -if turns into -ive.

mistakes.why: This leaves the adjective in its masculine -if form, but grand-mère is feminine.
Adding a plain e to -if is the usual guess; the f has to change first.
The feminine ending is right but the s makes it plural, and there is one grandmother.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: It’s a serious question. Leave the wrong adjective tile unused.
exercises.hint: Question is feminine. Use the feminine of sérieux.
exercises.feedback: One adjective tile is the masculine form. Choose the one that matches une question.
exercises.explanation: Sérieux becomes sérieuse in the feminine, like heureux and heureuse.

mistakes.why: That tile is the masculine form. Une question is feminine, so the -eux ending has to change.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of italien.
exercises.hint: Voisine is feminine singular. Adjectives ending in -en double a letter before the e.
exercises.feedback: Check both the doubled consonant and the number.
exercises.explanation: Italien becomes italienne: -en doubles the n before adding e. Voisine is singular, so no s.

mistakes.why: That is the masculine form. Ma voisine is a woman, so the adjective needs its feminine ending.
The e is there but the n was not doubled, and -en adjectives double that consonant first.
The feminine spelling is right, but the s makes it plural and there is one neighbour.

exercises.instruction: Write bon in the form that agrees with soupe. Write only the adjective.
exercises.hint: Soupe is feminine singular. Adjectives ending in -on double the last consonant before e.
exercises.feedback: Just adding e is not enough for -on adjectives.
exercises.explanation: Bon becomes bonne in the feminine: the n doubles, then e is added.

mistakes.why: That is the masculine form. La soupe is a feminine noun.
The e was added without doubling the n; -on adjectives double that consonant in the feminine.
The feminine spelling is right, but the s makes it plural and there is one soup.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.hint: Fille is feminine. Gentil doubles its last consonant in the feminine.
exercises.feedback: Check the spelling of the feminine: one letter is doubled.
exercises.explanation: Gentil becomes gentille in the feminine, with a double l.

mistakes.why: Gentil is the masculine form. Fille is feminine, and this adjective doubles its last consonant before the e.
There is only one l here. The consonant has to be doubled before the feminine e.
Fille is a feminine noun, so the article in front of it must be feminine.

exercises.instruction: Replace Mon cousin with Ma cousine and make canadien agree.
exercises.hint: Canadien ends in -en, like italien.
exercises.feedback: Change both the noun phrase and the adjective, and check the doubled letter.
exercises.explanation: Canadien becomes canadienne: -en becomes -enne in the feminine.

mistakes.why: The noun phrase became feminine but the adjective stayed masculine; -en adjectives take a doubled n plus e.
The e was added without doubling the n, which is what this ending asks for first.
Cousine is feminine, so the possessive in front of it must be the feminine one.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: It’s a traditional party. One tile is misspelled; leave it unused.
exercises.hint: Fête is feminine. Adjectives ending in -el double the l before e.
exercises.feedback: Compare the two adjective tiles letter by letter.
exercises.explanation: Traditionnel becomes traditionnelle in the feminine: -el becomes -elle.

mistakes.why: That tile has a single l. Adjectives in -el double the l before the feminine e.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of blanc.
exercises.hint: Robe is feminine singular. Blanc has an unusual feminine.
exercises.feedback: Blanc does not simply add e in the feminine, and there is only one dress.
exercises.explanation: Blanc becomes blanche in the feminine. One dress, so no s.

mistakes.why: That is the masculine form. Robe is feminine, and this adjective has an irregular feminine rather than a simple added e.
That form is masculine and plural. There is one dress and it is feminine.
The feminine spelling is right, but the s makes it plural and une robe is a single dress.

exercises.instruction: Write long in the form that agrees with route. Write only the adjective.
exercises.hint: Route is feminine. Long needs an extra letter before the e to keep its sound.
exercises.feedback: Just adding e is not the right spelling here.
exercises.explanation: Long becomes longue in the feminine: a u is added before the e.

mistakes.why: That is the masculine form. La route is feminine, and this adjective needs an extra letter before the e.
A plain e after the g softens the sound. A letter is missing between the g and the e.
The feminine spelling is right, but the s makes it plural and there is one road.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.hint: Eau is feminine. Frais has an irregular feminine.
exercises.feedback: The feminine of frais is not fraise (that is a strawberry).
exercises.explanation: Frais becomes fraîche in the feminine (fraiche in the reformed spelling). Eau is feminine, and la becomes l’ before the vowel.

mistakes.why: Frais is the masculine form. Eau is feminine, and this adjective has an irregular feminine.
Une fraise is a strawberry. This feminine is not built by adding e to the masculine.
The adjective is fine, but la loses its a before a vowel and takes an apostrophe.

exercises.instruction: Fix the adjective.
exercises.hint: Rue is feminine. Long has a special feminine spelling.
exercises.feedback: The adjective is still masculine. Watch the spelling of the feminine.
exercises.explanation: Rue is feminine singular, so long becomes longue.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged, with the masculine form still in place, although rue is feminine.
A plain e after the g is not enough: another letter is needed to keep the hard g sound.
The plural s does not belong: cette rue is one single street.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of rouge.
exercises.hint: Rouge already ends in e.
exercises.feedback: Do not add a second e, and there is only one car.
exercises.explanation: Adjectives that already end in e, like rouge, do not change in the feminine.

mistakes.why: An extra e was added for the feminine, but this adjective already ends in e and takes nothing more.
The s marks a plural. Ma voiture is one car.

exercises.instruction: Replace Mon frère with Ma sœur and make the adjective agree.
exercises.hint: Jeune already ends in e. What does it need in the feminine?
exercises.feedback: Change the noun phrase. Check whether the adjective really needs another letter.
exercises.explanation: Jeune is the same in the masculine and the feminine, so only the noun phrase changes.

mistakes.why: A second e was added for the feminine, but an adjective already ending in e does not change.
The s marks a plural and there is one sister.
Sœur is feminine, so the possessive in front of it must be the feminine one.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.hint: Leçon is feminine, but facile already ends in e.
exercises.feedback: Do not add anything to facile for a single feminine noun.
exercises.explanation: Facile ends in e, so it is the same for masculine and feminine singular.

mistakes.why: An extra e was added for the feminine, but this adjective already ends in e.
The s marks a plural and the sentence names one lesson.
Leçon is a feminine noun, so the article in front of it must be feminine.

exercises.instruction: Fix the adjective. Sœurs is plural.
exercises.hint: Jeune does not change for the feminine, but it still marks the plural.
exercises.feedback: The adjective needs a plural ending.
exercises.explanation: An adjective ending in e stays the same in the feminine but still adds s in the plural: jeunes.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged. The adjective does not change for the feminine, but it still has to mark the plural.
An extra e was added as if for the feminine; this adjective never takes one, and that is not what is missing.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of loyal. Amis is masculine plural.
exercises.hint: Masculine adjectives ending in -al have a special plural.
exercises.feedback: Loyal does not just add s in the masculine plural.
exercises.explanation: In the masculine plural, -al becomes -aux: loyal, loyaux.

mistakes.why: This adds the regular s, but masculine adjectives in -al do not build their plural that way.
That is the singular form. Mes amis names several people.
That is the feminine plural. The prompt says amis is masculine, so the e does not belong.

exercises.instruction: Write normal in the form that agrees with problèmes. Write only the adjective.
exercises.hint: Problèmes is masculine plural, and normal ends in -al.
exercises.feedback: The plural of -al adjectives in the masculine is not -als.
exercises.explanation: Normal becomes normaux in the masculine plural: -al becomes -aux.

mistakes.why: Masculine -al adjectives do not take a plain s in the plural: the ending itself changes.
That is the singular form. Problèmes names several problems.
That is the feminine plural. Problème is a masculine noun.

exercises.instruction: Make the whole sentence plural (le becomes les).
exercises.hint: The noun and the adjective both end in -eau. Words in -eau do not take s in the plural.
exercises.feedback: Make the article, the noun, the verb and the adjective plural.
exercises.explanation: Words ending in -eau add x in the plural: gâteaux, beaux. The verb becomes sont.

mistakes.why: Words ending in -eau take x in the plural, not s.
The article, the noun and the verb went plural, but the adjective was left singular.
The subject is plural now, so the verb has to be plural as well.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.hint: Journal and local both end in -al, and both change the same way in the plural.
exercises.feedback: Check the plural of both the noun and the adjective.
exercises.explanation: Masculine -al becomes -aux in the plural: journal, journaux; local, locaux.

mistakes.why: Both words end in -al in the singular, and that ending does not simply take an s in the plural.
The noun is plural but the adjective was left in the singular.
That is the feminine plural. Journal is a masculine noun.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: I have loyal friends (the friends are all women). Leave the wrong adjective tiles unused.
exercises.hint: The -aux plural is only for the masculine. The feminine follows the regular pattern.
exercises.feedback: Amies is feminine plural. Pick the adjective with the feminine e and the plural s.
exercises.explanation: The feminine plural of loyal is regular: loyale, loyales. Only the masculine plural becomes loyaux.

mistakes.why: The -aux plural belongs to masculine nouns only. Amies with an e names women.
That tile is a masculine plural that does not even exist, and the noun here is feminine anyway.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of délicieux. Gâteaux is masculine plural.
exercises.hint: Délicieux already ends in x.
exercises.feedback: A masculine adjective ending in x cannot take another plural letter.
exercises.explanation: Adjectives ending in -s or -x do not change in the masculine plural: délicieux.

mistakes.why: An s was added to a word that already ends in x. A masculine adjective in -x takes no second plural letter.
That is the feminine singular. Gâteaux is masculine and names several cakes.
That is the feminine plural. Gâteau is a masculine noun, so the feminine ending is wrong.

exercises.instruction: Write gris in the form that agrees with chats. Chats is masculine plural. Write only the adjective.
exercises.hint: Look at the last letter of gris.
exercises.feedback: Nothing needs to be added for a masculine plural here.
exercises.explanation: An adjective ending in s stays the same in the masculine plural: des chats gris.

mistakes.why: A second s was added to a word that already ends in one. Nothing is added in the masculine plural here.
That is the feminine singular. The prompt says chats is masculine, and there are two of them.
That is the feminine plural. Chat is a masculine noun.

exercises.instruction: Fix the adjective. Voisins is masculine plural.
exercises.hint: Look at the last letter of heureux before you add anything.
exercises.feedback: The masculine plural of heureux looks the same as the singular.
exercises.explanation: Adjectives ending in -x never add s: heureux is both singular and plural.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged, with an s stuck onto a word that already ends in x.
That is the feminine plural. Voisins is masculine, so the feminine ending is wrong.
That is the feminine singular: wrong gender, and it drops the plural as well.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.hint: Look at the last letter of français. In French, nationality adjectives take no capital letter.
exercises.feedback: Check the adjective ending: it already ends in s.
exercises.explanation: Français does not change in the masculine plural because it already ends in s.

mistakes.why: An s was added to a word that already ends in s; the plural letter is there from the start.
That is the feminine plural. Garçons names boys, so the masculine form is needed.
That is the feminine singular: wrong gender and wrong number for several boys.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of marron.
exercises.hint: Marron is also the name of a chestnut. Colour words taken from nouns follow their own rule.
exercises.feedback: This colour word never changes, whatever the noun.
exercises.explanation: Marron is invariable: it takes no e and no s, even with feminine plural chaussures.

mistakes.why: The plural s treats this like an ordinary adjective. A colour word that is also the name of a nut never takes an ending.
This invents a feminine with a doubled n. This colour word does not agree at all.
This piles a feminine and a plural ending onto a colour word that takes neither.

exercises.instruction: Write orange in the form that agrees with sacs. Write only the adjective.

alternatives.message: Accepted: you will see oranges too. The standard rule keeps colour words that come from nouns, like orange and marron, invariable: des sacs orange.

exercises.hint: Orange is also a fruit. Colour words taken from nouns follow their own rule.
exercises.feedback: This colour word does not take a plural s.
exercises.explanation: Orange is invariable: des sacs orange.

mistakes.why: These invent an accented ending for a colour word borrowed from the name of a fruit. Such colour words keep one single form.
Only the adjective goes in the blank; the words around it are already in the sentence.

exercises.instruction: Fix the adjective.
exercises.hint: Some colour words never take a plural s.
exercises.feedback: Yeux is plural, but this colour word stays the same.
exercises.explanation: Marron is invariable, so les yeux marron has no s on marron.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged, with the plural s still on a colour word taken from the name of a nut.
These add feminine endings to a colour word that never changes, and yeux is masculine anyway.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: We have orange curtains. Leave the wrong adjective tile unused.
exercises.hint: Orange is a colour word taken from a noun.
exercises.feedback: One adjective tile has a plural s it should not have.
exercises.explanation: Orange does not agree, so rideaux orange has no s on orange.

mistakes.why: That tile carries a plural s. A colour word borrowed from the name of a fruit keeps one form with every noun.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of content.
exercises.hint: Paul is a man and Marie is a woman. What does a mixed group take?
exercises.feedback: A mixed group does not use the feminine form.
exercises.explanation: A mixed group takes the masculine plural: contents.

mistakes.why: That is the singular form. Paul et Marie are two people.
That is the feminine singular: a group of two is neither one person nor all women.
That is the feminine plural. As soon as one man belongs to the group, French drops the feminine.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.source: My brother and my sister are tall (grand).
answers: Mon frère et ma sœur sont grands.
Ma sœur et mon frère sont grands.
spellingAnswers: Mon frère et ma soeur sont grands.
Ma soeur et mon frère sont grands.
exercises.hint: The adjective describes a man and a woman together.
exercises.feedback: With a mixed group, the adjective does not take the feminine e.
exercises.explanation: Frère and sœur together form a mixed group, which takes the masculine plural: grands.

answers: Mon frère et ma sœur sont grandes.
Mon frère et ma soeur sont grandes.
mistakes.why: That is the feminine plural, but the group includes a brother, and one man cancels the feminine.

answers: Mon frère et ma sœur sont grand.
Mon frère et ma soeur sont grand.
mistakes.why: The adjective is singular while it describes two people.

answers: Mon frère et ma sœur est grand.
Mon frère et ma soeur est grand.
mistakes.why: Two subjects joined by et take a plural verb, and the adjective is left singular too.

exercises.instruction: Change the subject to Julie et Marc and make the verb and the adjective agree.
exercises.hint: Adding Marc makes a mixed group.
exercises.feedback: The verb becomes plural, and the adjective needs the form for a mixed group.
exercises.explanation: Julie et Marc is a mixed group, so fatigué takes the masculine plural: fatigués.

mistakes.why: This keeps the feminine ending of the original sentence, but Marc puts a man in the group.
The adjective is still singular while the subject now names two people.
Two people joined by et need a plural verb, and the adjective has to follow.

exercises.instruction: Fix the adjective.
exercises.source: Mon père et ma mère sont sérieuses.
answers: Mon père et ma mère sont sérieux.
exercises.hint: The group has one man and one woman.
exercises.feedback: A mixed group never takes the feminine plural.
exercises.explanation: A mixed group takes the masculine plural. Sérieux already ends in x, so it does not change.

answers: Mon père et ma mère sont sérieuses.
mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged: the feminine plural was taken from ma mère alone, ignoring mon père.

answers: Mon père et ma mère sont sérieuse.
mistakes.why: Feminine and singular: wrong on both counts for two people, one of them a man.

answers: Mon père et ma mère sont sérieuxs.
mistakes.why: An s was added to a word that already ends in x; that ending never takes one.
